correctness.rationale: Verified full RESULT.md against Chuah 2026 Theorem 1.1 equations (1.13)-(1.14). For p=n-2, H_p is quotient of positive integrals over [R1,x] and [x+R,R2]; p^{-1} factors cancel for p>0, and p=0 gives exact logarithmic formula. Both intervals are nonempty for x in (R1,R2-R), with finite endpoints R1>R>0. H_p is increasing from 0 to infinity in x, so the level alpha=M1/M2>0 has a unique interior solution. Differentiating under finite integrals gives d_p log H_p=E_upper(log s)-E_lower(log s)>0, since every s on the second interval exceeds every s on the first by at least R. With x-monotonicity this forces r_{n+1}<r_n including n=2 to3. For p>0 exact equality yields 1-(1+delta/R1)^(-p)=alpha*(R1/(R1+R+delta))^p*[1-((R1+R+delta)/R2)^p]. Bound by alpha*q^p with q=R1/(R1+R)<1; using -log(1-t), obtain p log(1+delta/R1)->0, thus p delta/R1->0. Fixed strict R1+R<R2 gives the outer-endpoint factor->1; p delta->0 yields the middle factor->1, while left side~p delta/R1. Hence delta~alpha*R1*q^p/p. Covers n>=2, positive boundary data, fixed R>0 and strict annular gap. No numerical extrapolation or unproved PDE existence is asserted beyond the cited source.

value.rationale: The annular PDE model is a naturally dimension-indexed family, and understanding how a fixed interaction separation redistributes its two interfaces is a meaningful structural comparison, not an arbitrary finite parameter slice. The theorem gives strict order uniformly across every integer dimension and a sharp leading exponentially small boundary-layer width and prefactor. These are quantitative information beyond fixed-n uniqueness and the R->0 transition. The derivation is short and grounded in elementary radial potential integrals, so value is bounded to this annular family and not presented as a general free-boundary theorem or a new PDE technique.
